question: Should the synthetic project adopt the shared index?
answer: Adopt with conditions, not unconditionally. The synthetic pilot supports adoption [s1][s2], but a privacy dissent [s3] and the absence of independent external validation [s6] remain. A federated alternative [s4] should be compared, and the earlier adoption decision was reversed [s8]. Do not treat this as a team decision.

evidence.title: Pilot latency note
evidence.text: The synthetic pilot reduced median search time by 18% across two projects.

evidence.title: Cost estimate
evidence.text: The synthetic cost estimate is two engineer-weeks for the first rollout.

dissent.title: Privacy objection
dissent.text: A pilot participant reports that a private note appeared in the index and the opt-out was not honoured.

alternatives.title: Federated alternative
alternatives.text: A federated index could keep each project local while sharing only explicit references.

unresolved.title: Missing external validation
unresolved.text: No independent external validation of the synthetic pilot exists.

revision.title: Revision note
revision.text: An earlier synthetic decision to adopt was reversed after the privacy incident; the revision remains visible.

limits: Synthetic project authored for Week03; not a real team or real index.
The responder is deterministic; no model, no network, no provider.
The slice is read-only over synthetic evidence and session state; it writes no authority state.
